clue.text: Hide in the grass, having got stronger

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of the other, as the clue says hide sits in the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
to hide something is to cover it up

explanation.surface: Someone lies low in long grass and comes out feeling stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a noun (an animal's skin or a bird-watcher's shelter) but is the verb, and 'in' is the container signal, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover from illness is to regain strength, so a recovered person has got stronger again.

clue.text: Swift passer-by starting to interrupt robbery

indicators.note: the start of passer-by breaks into the robbery word, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a raid is a robbery, as on a bank

indicators.note: only the opening letter of passer-by is used

explanation.surface: A quick bystander breaks up a robbery in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes P from passer-by and 'to interrupt' puts it into RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms, both meaning very fast.

clue.text: Catches party where there are police

parts.note: to cop is slang for to catch, so catches gives cops
a hop is an informal dance or party

explanation.surface: A raid nabs a party, which is the local nick in action.
explanation.walkthrough: A COP SHOP is informal British slang for a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a police station, the place where police officers are based.

clue.text: Judge's attitude

definitions.meaning: to judge something is to ... it in a certain way, to regard it
an attitude is a ..., an opinion one holds

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to judge or regard; as a noun it means an opinion or outlook.

clue.text: Womaniser loses love in Italy

indicators.note: a piece is dropped from the womaniser word, signalled by losing

parts.note: a Romeo is a womaniser, after Shakespeare's lover
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A ladies' man gets dumped while holidaying in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' removes O (love) from ROMEO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian capital is a city in Italy, so the definition locates it by country.

clue.text: Do as you please! I need no baby-sitter!

definitions.meaning: a phrase telling someone to carry on regardless of oneself
to mind a child is to babysit it, so this is a plea not to be minded

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both waves someone on to do as they wish and, read literally, refuses minding like a child.

clue.text: Graduate backstage gets bread roll

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: the stage word is read backwards, signalled by back

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A graduate working behind the scenes is handed a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backstage' must be split: 'back' is the reversal signal and 'stage' the word reversed, giving GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked.

clue.text: Bribe former worker with hesitation

parts.note: back can mean earlier or former, as in back issues
a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A bribe is offered hesitantly to an ex-employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is a slang term for a bribe paid secretly.

clue.text: Covered with fat when consumed by gluttony

indicators.note: one piece is swallowed inside the other, as food is consumed

parts.note: greed is gluttony, excessive appetite
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Fat everywhere is the result of being eaten up by gluttony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is easily passed over as a link word, but it supplies letters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Greased describes something smeared with fat or grease.

clue.text: Had sample moulded for translucent cover

indicators.note: moulded means shaped anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shaped a sample into a see-through cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moulded' rearranges HADSAMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampshade is a cover over a bulb, often translucent so light passes through.

clue.text: Sweet spice with perfect taste

parts.note: pepper is a spice
in mint condition means perfect, as new
cream as the finest, choicest part, the best of good taste

explanation.surface: A sweet that combines spice with a perfect flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is a noun here: a confectionery item.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mint-flavoured fondant confection, a type of sweet.

clue.text: Children's author had turned left

indicators.note: turned means the word had is read the other way round

explanation.surface: A writer for children did a left turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses HAD to DAH. Roald Dahl wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl is a famous British writer of children's books.

clue.text: Force hemp to be unravelled by a half-sister

indicators.note: unravelling rope fibres loosens them, so these letters are rearranged
the hyphenated half-sister splits, and half keeps only the front three letters of sister

explanation.surface: Hemp rope is pulled apart by a stepsister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be unravelled' turns HEMP into EMPH. 'half-sister' is not a relative: split it, so 'half' takes the first half of sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is force or stress given to a word or point.

clue.text: Indecent film exposed in the Guardian, for example

parts.note: broad humour is coarse or indecent
a film is a thin sheet of material

explanation.surface: A blue movie is exposed in a newspaper's pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed in' is padding linking wordplay to definition. The Guardian was formerly a large-format newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a large-format newspaper, and the Guardian was long one.

clue.text: Of course this is the last hole

definitions.text: Of course this is the last hole

parts.words: Of course this is the last hole
parts.note: read 'course' as a golf course: the final hole of a full round

explanation.definitionFit: A full round of golf has eighteen holes, so the final one has this ordinal.

clue.text: When one appears in person, it's slander

parts.note: as can mean when

indicators.note: the one word turns up inside the person word, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A personal appearance turns out to be slanderous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is only a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast aspersions is to slander; an aspersion is a damaging remark.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvres make Anita spit

indicators.note: make here means form into, so these letters are built into something new

explanation.surface: Starters so bad they make a diner named Anita spit them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges ANITASPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian starters, the equivalent of hors d'oeuvres.

clue.text: Russian girl in North America at daybreak

indicators.note: break means smash up, so the letters of day are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian girl arrives in North America at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daybreak' must be split: 'break' rearranges 'day' into DYA. 'in' and 'at' are link words. Nadya is short for Nadezhda.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadya is a Russian girl's name, a pet form of Nadezhda.

clue.text: Sinatra label covered "Expression of Joy"

indicators.note: covered means held within, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: Sinatra's record label covered a song called Expression of Joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' points to TRALA inside SinaTRA LAbel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a sung exclamation expressing gaiety or joy.

clue.text: A k-king's attentive

parts.note: a stammered king, so a stammered King Lear's: L-Lear's

explanation.surface: Someone stammers about a king who is listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'k-king' tells you to stutter the king's name: King Lear becomes L-Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all ears is an idiom for listening very attentively.

clue.text: At home, mater treated foot problem

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mother at home treated someone's ailing foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges HOMEMATER. 'At' is a link. Mater is old British slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammertoe is a deformity where a toe bends permanently, a foot ailment.

clue.text: Blast makes insect hide in bracken

indicators.note: the insect hides inside the bracken word, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: tara is a bracken fern of New Zealand
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect conceals itself among bracken.
explanation.walkthrough: TARA is an obscure word: a New Zealand bracken fern, known mostly to crossword solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantara is a fanfare, a blast on a trumpet or horn.

clue.text: Bright foreign editor

parts.note: Polish, from Poland, is one kind of foreign

explanation.surface: A clever editor from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished means shining and bright, as a buffed surface.

clue.text: Native South American partly incapacitated

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the word incapacitated is used

explanation.surface: An indigenous South American is somewhat incapacitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' points to the start of INCApacitated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were native South American people of the Andes.

clue.text: Help hound hiding its head

indicators.note: the hound word loses its front letter, as a head hidden from view

parts.note: a basset is a short-legged hound

explanation.surface: A dog's help is offered while it hides its face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding its head' removes the B of BASSET.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a help, a useful or valuable thing.

clue.text: Doctor, one that stops a horse

parts.note: Doctor Who is the TV time-traveller, so Doctor gives who
a means one

explanation.surface: A doctor is the one who halts a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a long-running British TV science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the command called out to make a horse stop.

clue.text: Personalities, for example, getting very large

parts.note: OS, outsize, labels very large clothing

explanation.surface: Celebrities are getting very big.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego means the self, so egos are personalities or selves.

clue.text: Improperly ask Athens singer, one involved in deception

indicators.note: improperly means wrongly arranged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly approaches a singer from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improperly' rearranges ASKATHENSSINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake in the grass is a treacherous person, a hidden deceiver.

clue.text: Insect caught short — it's in the corner

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the insect word is missing a piece

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An insect has been trapped in the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes C (caught) from INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture set in a corner of a larger map or page.

clue.text: Manager's sharp, which is an initial advantage

parts.note: a head is a manager or boss, with the possessive giving s
tart means sharp or sour in taste

explanation.surface: A boss is sharp, which gives an early lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage given at the beginning of a race or task.
